summary: One uniform cap family controls all points in local compact finite Gauss-fibre families, giving uniform maximizing-net convergence there. The required Shilov-neighborhood basis remains unproved.
detailedSummary: Fixed Laurent initials and a finite-flat singleton-Gauss representative yield properness concentration. Compact parameter bounds give one collar and epsilon, uniformly bounded cap energies, and atom coefficients at least epsilon squared at every fibre point. Nonordered moments imply uniform convergence. Shrinking radial polyannuli need not fit ordinary target neighborhoods, so this does not resolve upper control or representability.
text:
This uses earlier own notes n1 and n2, at their explicit bounded analytic-foundation boundary. It proves a LOCAL UNIFORM FINITE-GAUSS-FIBRE sector of the proposed geometric route; it does not construct the required Shilov-neighborhood basis or solve analytic representability.

Fix a full graded-dimension-two point x. Use the SAME two fixed Laurent polynomials P1,P2 and compact finite-flat representative f:V->U from n1, with positive degree D and singleton Gauss fibre {x} at g0=f(x). V,U are analytic neighborhoods, so x and g0 lie in their ordinary interiors. Choose a small compact rectangle J of log radii around g0 whose continuous weighted Gauss section sigma(J) lies in Int U. The section is only a continuous topological map, not asserted analytic. Properness gives a stronger concentration assertion: for any ordinary neighborhood O of x, V\O is compact and f(V\O) is compact and avoids g0 by the singleton fibre. A target neighborhood of g0 avoids that image. Shrinking J makes every point of Theta=f^-1(sigma(J)) cap V lie in O. In particular choose O inside Int V and inside a small inner base-coordinate tropical ball. Theta is compact, and every point in its finite fibres has full graded dimension two because its complete residue field is finite over the two-dimensional weighted Gauss field.

Uniform cap construction. On a larger injective base tropical ball of radius R, put rho0=|tau-tau(x)|^2/2 and psi_r=logmax(1,|P1|/r1,|P2|/r2). Laurent polynomials are bounded on the compact larger polyannulus and r_i have positive minima on J. Thus 0<=psi_r<=M0 uniformly. Choose one delta>0 below R^2/4 and one epsilon>0 with delta+epsilon M0 less than the minimum of rho0 on a fixed outer collar. Every w_r=max(0,delta+epsilon psi_r-rho0), extended by zero, is an actual global continuous member of C; n1's capped logarithm and maximum construction also verifies the polynomial-zero points. Uniformly 0<=w_r<=M=delta+epsilon M0. Shrink J by properness so Theta lies where rho0<delta/2. On this inner region theta_w_r=epsilon DDpsi_r.

At EVERY point y of each finite Gauss fibre, CLD18.6.2 and finite-flat calibration14.5.2–3 give the local log-max top mass d_y delta_y, where d_y is the positive integer local degree and sum_y d_y=D. This is the actual fibre current on ordinary boundaryless interiors, at the same raw convention as n1's atom. Therefore MA(w_r)>=epsilon^2 d_y delta_y>=epsilon^2 delta_y. This coefficient is uniform in r,y; no extra varying-ground-field factor is inserted. Normalize w_hat_r=w_r-sup w_r. Since -M<=w_hat_r<=0, energy monotonicity gives E(w_hat_r)>=-2M uniformly.

For any a,b in C_C set D0=max(C,2M,0). The fixed-test absolute estimate and the6D0 gradient bounds in n1 give, uniformly in r,
integral|a-b|MA(w_r)<=Omega_C(I)+2sqrt(6D0)sqrt(Psi_D0(I)).
Divide by epsilon^2 at each fibre atom to bound |a(y)-b(y)| uniformly over Theta. For full-dual maximizing tails, n2 gives I<=4(epsilon_a+epsilon_b)->0. Thus their restrictions are uniformly Cauchy on compact Theta. Completeness of C(Theta,R) gives a finite continuous uniform limit equal to the full-point tuple. No metrizability is needed. Its continuity, together with the proved concentration of nearby finite Gauss fibres at x, controls its values along this family near x.

The remaining step is not supplied. An ordinary target neighborhood of a Gauss point can exclude cancellation points with the SAME coordinate radii. Therefore shrinking coordinate polyannuli need not lie in U. Pulling them back through this LOCAL finite-flat representative does not construct the affinoid neighborhoods needed for the all-Shilov formula. Properness and this uniform cap family alone do not prove that all required Shilov boundaries belong to Theta. Consequently this result does not imply equality between the full-point tuple and its USC upper relaxation, positivity, generated membership, or the prescribed equation. The entire proof and this limitation are in scoped-paper.tex, Proposition uniformfibres; all primary foundations remain as in n1.
